chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Safwan,wan from Ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who cut his hair while he was in the state of Ihram for Tamattu', then arrived in Mecca, completed his ritual, released the binding of his head, trimmed (his hair), anointed himself, and emerged from Ihram. He said: 'Upon him is the blood of a sheep.'

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: Emerged from the state of Ihram
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: The blood of a sheep (a type of sacrificial expiation)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٌ: One performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.نُسُكَهُ: His ritual/sacrifice (referring to the completion of Hajj rites)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for cutting hair prematurely during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that a pilgrim in the state of *Tamattu'* who prematurely cuts their hair (*taqsir*) before completing the Hajj rites incurs a penalty of *dam*, specifically the slaughter of a sheep. This ruling highlights the strict adherence to the sequence of rituals in Shia jurisprudence, where the early termination of the state of *ihram* necessitates a tangible expiation to validate the pilgrimage.
